answer: Reputation Prism Split. Each identity's influence is capped by a decaying credit score the network recomputes at every dawn from its interaction history; new identities start near zero, so spinning up N of them yields N near-zero weights while honest accounts accrue weight over weeks. An attacker must fund sustained, non-reciprocal activity on each identity long enough to clear the decay threshold. Every false node also consumes timber—real storage and bandwidth for its share of message relaying—so marginal cost per identity rises with fleet size instead of staying flat.
